definition: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.
example: One anomalous vote interrupted the unanimous pattern.
nuance: Anomalous describes deviation and does not itself explain the cause.
prompt: A scientist checks an unusual measurement.
options: The anomalous reading differed sharply from every previous result.
The anomalous reading exactly matched the expected pattern.
The reading was anomalous because it was typical.
Anomalous meant the scientist disliked the reading.
reasons: Departure from the established pattern is anomalous.
A personal preference does not establish an anomaly.

practice.prompt: A birdwatcher keeps a log of the birds she sees all winter.
options: A hummingbird at her feeder in January was an anomalous sighting so far north.
The sparrows that showed up at dawn every single day were the most anomalous birds on her list.
The two finches seemed anomalous, since their beaks and songs were identical in every way.
She signed her log with a made-up name so the bird club would treat it as anomalous.
reasons: A warm-weather bird turning up in midwinter breaks the expected seasonal pattern.
Birds that arrive predictably every day are the norm, not an exception to it.
Closely matching each other suggests analogous; nothing here departs from a norm.
Hiding one's name makes a report anonymous, a look-alike word with a different meaning.
